newsitem.title: ITALY: POLL-ITALY AUGUST CPI SEEN FLAT YEAR ON YEAR.
newsitem.headline: POLL-ITALY AUGUST CPI SEEN FLAT YEAR ON YEAR.

text.p: Italy's yearly consumer price inflation should remain unchanged on July's 1.6 percent rate even if a slight month on month rise is expected, a Reuters poll showed.
But the 10 analysts surveyed agreed that the major unknown factor was the impact of petrol prices.
Those polled on average saw August CPI rising 0.1 percent month on month and a yearly rate of 1.6 percent.

In July, CPI inflation stayed flat monthly and rose 1.6 percent annually, the first rise in headline inflation in a year. In August 1996, prices rose 0.1 percent monthly and rose 3.4 percent annually.
Preliminary CPI data for August from 11 sample Italian cities will be published on August 21 and 22 and national statistics institute Istat will announce the final national figure on September 4.

Paolo Casadio, economist at Credito Italiano, forecast a monthly increase of between 0.1 and 0.2 percent depending on the number of petrol companies cutting their pump prices before Istat collates the August figure.
At the beginning of August petrol prices rose in line with a strong rise in the dollar which last week touched a high of 1,850 lire.

On Monday, Italian energy group Eni said its petrol distributors Agip Petroli and Ip were reducing their petrol and diesel prices by 10 lire a litre and on Tuesday Tamoil announced a similar reduction. At 1346 GMT, the dollar was quoted at 1,817.85/8.15 lire.

"Apart from the uncertainty of the impact of petrol prices, in August we will only partially see the effect of the strong dollar but this will be more worrisome in September when industrial price list reviews take place," Casadio said.

"The petrol price rises have been greater than the last reductions. Other companies will probably reduce their prices but this won't likely affect the August index, said Bruno Rovelli, economist at Citibank.
The analysts saw the petrol price rise having an impact of 0.03 percent on the monthly index.
"We will have to see if and by how much the other energy companies cut their petrol and petroleum product prices," said Stefano Lelli, economist at Banco di Sardegna.

For Pio De Gregorio, economist at NatWest, "the campaign of phone call discounts by state operator Telecom Italia and the extension of those given by national carrier Alitalia and private airline AirOne will counterbalance the petrol price hikes", therefore helping to limit the rise in consumer prices.
